utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone in this courtroom. Ms. Pilipovic, I think we ended yesterday in a brief discussion on Rule 90(H). You may proceed, in strict observance of Rule 90(H), with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me start off by thanking you for your guidance. I should like to stress - and I hope this won't take more than two minutes of my time - that the Defence has been before this Trial Chamber and in this Tribunal for quite some time. It has always been ready for cross-examination, which always evolved in harmony with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Let me stress that the Defence has been confronted with a serious problem, but in keeping with guidance from the Chamber, it will adhere to 90(H)(ii), which gives the Defence the right, if the witness is able to give evidence relevant to the case, for the cross-examining party to ask questions to the subject matter of that case, and in keeping with your suggestions and adhering to Rule 90(H)(ii), I shall continue my cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday during the cross-examination, we left off discussing the fact that you were within the reserve formation of the police force. You explained to us that you had returned your rifle and uniform which you were issued with, and that took place in 1991. Yesterday, asked by my learned colleague - and that was at 15 hours, 38 minutes, 11 seconds, and also in lines 8 and 10 - you spoke about the fact that at Grbavica, the civilian police force had set up its headquarters, as well as the military police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now tell me when the headquarters of the civilian police force was set up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very beginning - I can't quite tell you the day - which means in June 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters are having difficulties hearing the witness. We apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we -- is this a technical problem or is this a matter of speaking more closely to the microphone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. D, would you please speak in the microphone so that everyone can hear you well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the headquarters of the civilian police was located? Where was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The civilian police headquarters was in Zagrebacka Street and in the former nursery school building.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the only headquarters that existed, or were there several headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the civilian police?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We're talking about the civilian police force now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was just that one civilian police headquarters at Grbavica 1, which is where I was. As for the other parts of town, I really can't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. D, may I ask you to look at your screen and wait until the text is not moving any more before answering, because the translation needs some time, and since you are speaking the same language, it goes too quick. So just look at the screen. Once it stops, then you give the answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You say that you know that there was one headquarters of the civilian police force and that it was located in Zagrebacka Street; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Grbavica region, there was just one headquarters of the civilian police at Grbavica, and the main headquarters also existed in Lukavica at the location where the Energoinvest company once was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you visit that headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When the headquarters were set up -- when was it set up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When did you visit the headquarters for the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the role of the members of the Civil Defence or civilian police was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what their role was, but I do know that those civilian policemen stood at two locations, were positioned in two locations at that part of Grbavica where I was. One checkpoint was at the intersection going on to Vrace, and the other checkpoint was at the intersection above Vrace, the intersection of the road going to Trbevic and Lukavac.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you would see members of the civilian police, would you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would. I saw them every day.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wearing blue uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What sort of weapons did they have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had an automatic rifle of the 762 type, and most of them had pistols with them as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You've already said that you saw them at the checkpoints. Do you happen to know what their role was there? What were they doing there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had the right to stop vehicles at the checkpoint and to control the passing of vehicles and to check out the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you talked to them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you, while you were chatting to them, why they were controlling those checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never asked them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you previously, and I'm talking about the time before the headquarters of the civilian police was set up, whether the civilian police had positions at those particular locations? Did you see them ever?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me mention that until I had joined the army, I didn't leave my house at all. I didn't walk around anywhere because it was dangerous. So I don't know the answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You've just said that you never left the house because it was dangerous. Could you tell us what, according to you, was the danger? What did the danger consist of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The very fact that I was of non-Serb ethnicity was a danger. There was always the possibility of somebody either beating me up or taking me off somewhere never to be heard of again.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did anybody mistreat you personally, physically, at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never, thank goodness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any other reason for which you stayed at home other than the fact that you thought it was dangerous?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the danger I've just talked about. I wasn't physically abused, but I was under a great deal of psychological pressure because of the existence of the types of danger that I mentioned a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You're a lawyer by profession, are you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were you working at the time? Were you employed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: What time do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Ah, yes. I apologise. I'm talking about June 1992, when you said you didn't dare go out of your house. So I'm asking you whether you were working, whether you were employed in 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I thought you were aware of the fact that in 1992, at Grbavica, nobody in Sarajevo, in that part of Sarajevo, went to work.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: But where were you employed? Where was your work post?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object to that question firstly on the ground of relevance, and secondly because the answer is likely to tend to identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I did hear Ms. Pilipovic well, she already rephrased the question by saying, "Where was your work post?" Would that be an acceptable question or would you object against it as well, apart from the relevance issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If she means by that, "Where physically, what part of town did you work?" I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There is still an issue of relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please, Ms. Pilipovic, explain to us what the relevance is of this question if it just looks at the location. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the question is relevant in view of the fact that the witness stressed that he sat at home and didn't go out anywhere. To my other question, he said that nobody worked in Sarajevo. I would just like to test the credibility of the witness's testimony, and I'd like to ask him to explain to us what part of town he worked in because of his limited movements. And he said that actually nobody in Sarajevo went to work. So all I want to know is the part of town he worked in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I see on my screen that the testimony was not that no one in Sarajevo went to work, but at Grbavica, in that part of Sarajevo, no one ever went to work. So of course you may test the credibility of the witness, but only on the basis of his testimony and not on an interpretation which does not stick to the wording of the testimony. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was your work post at Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: My work post was at Grbavica, and I said clearly that nobody in Sarajevo living at Grbavica went to work. I'm talking about Grbavica when I say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you know that at Grbavica, the inhabitants of Grbavica, even those working in Sarajevo, downtown Sarajevo, went to work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They could not go to work. They could not go into other parts of town because that was impossible.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Why was it impossible to go into other parts of town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was impossible because the front line had already been established on the bank of the Miljacka River and the Vrbanja Bridge and Bratstvo-Jedinstvo, and towards Hrasno and easterly towards Skenderija. You couldn't pass by that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You have just explained to us that the front line had been formed. Could you tell us when the line was set up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was set up in mid-May.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to the localities that you mentioned - Miljacka, the Vrbanja Most, the Bratstvo-Jedinstvo Bridge - who established the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb army.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to know that in other parts of town, a front line had also been formed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In respect to the other side of the Miljacka, was there a front line formed there too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume it was, on the basis of what I heard later on and what I learnt later on. I heard that it had been, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who formed that second front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bosnia-Herzegovina army. I apologise. At that time, in those initial phases, it was known as the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who made up the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina? What did it comprise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you explain what you mean by your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know which people made up the Territorial Defence of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean the ethnic composition, then I know that there were members of all three ethnic groups in it, but the majority were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in the Territorial Defence of the BH army, there were paramilitary formations as well within its composition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "paramilitary formations."

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You were a soldier, you did your military service, and I'm asking you now whether you know that, in Sarajevo, paramilitary units or formations existed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean the Territorial Defence, the Territorial Defence is not a paramilitary formation. It existed before the war as well. As to any other units, I am not aware of that, units that you perhaps consider were paramilitary. I wasn't there on the spot for me to be able to know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As to the Territorial Defence of the BH and the ethnic composition, how did you come by information about that? Did you learn that personally or via the media?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning, while the telephone lines were working, I was able to talk to members of my family who lived in other parts of town, and in talking to them, in my conversations with them, that's what I learnt. But let me also mention that they were people of different ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you that in those areas where they were when you were talking to them, that they were the Juka Prazina, Musan Topalovic, "Caco", Ismet Bajramovic, "Celo," paramilitary units and that they were ill-treating the inhabitants of Sarajevo? Did they tell you that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The question lacks any probative value, given that the witness has already said that he was not aware of the existence of any paramilitary groups within the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness's answer was that he had telephone conversations, and on the basis of those telephone conversations, he learnt who and what made up the Territorial Defence of the BH army. All I asked him was whether, through these telephone conversations with his relatives, he received information that there were paramilitary units in Sarajevo as well. All I want is a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied since the witness has testified that he did not know about paramilitary groups because he wasn't there, so he couldn't know. I think the question on whether this has been part of the telephone conversations may be asked. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you again: Did they say, over the phone, when talking to you, that there were paramilitary formations in Sarajevo: Musan Topalovic, "Caco," Ismet Bajramovic, "Celo"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That wasn't part of our telephone conversations, and during those telephone conversations, that was not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've just told us that you were able to contact your family members while the telephones were operating. When did you talk to your family -- when was the last time you talked to your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date, but it was sometime at the beginning of the war. I assume that it was up until mid-June when the lines were cut. So sometime in mid-June, but I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: May we take it, then, that in mid-June, at Grbavica, the telephone lines were down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: During your stay, and I'm going to be very precise, the period before you left Grbavica, which is 1993, I think it was May, the 23rd or 18th of May, whether at Grbavica there was -- whether Grbavica had electricity and water.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had electricity occasionally, but we had to take our water from the basement of the neighbouring building. So in our building there was no water in my parents' apartment. But where I lived before the war, that house did have water.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So during your -- while you lived at Grbavica, you and the inhabitants of Grbavica had problems with the power supply, water supply, and telephone lines; is that right? Would you agree with me there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The water problem wasn't as great as the electricity problem. And the telephones weren't working, as I said, from about mid-June until I left.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you spoke about the formation of the civilian police, you said that in that part of Grbavica where you lived, that the military police had also been set up. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The military police did exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the military police headquarters were located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Where was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police headquarters at Grbavica was located in the vicinity of the civilian police headquarters, about 200 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether there was just one headquarters or several of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was another headquarters of the military police somewhere at Vrace, around Petrovacka Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether at Vrace, where you say the headquarters of the military police was located, whether there was a police school or academy there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: That police school existed before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that the school existed before the war, could you tell me when? When was this before the war? What I'm asking you is when, according to you, did the war begin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you said you knew that the police school existed before the war, do you know why it ceased to exist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The school ceased to exist because of the fighting, because of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. war. I know that the children at that school, attending the school, were surrounded. An encirclement was formed round the school and for a time they were kept in the school building and then allowed to leave and go home. And from that time on, the school, as a police school, ceased to exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you said that the war began on the 6th of April, can you be more specific and tell us when the school was disbanded and when the children left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you that. I don't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that that was before the 6th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say whether it is correct or isn't correct because I don't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who surrounded the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb army did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see that for yourself? Did you see it personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it personally but I heard about it from a friend of mine who lives right up above that school. That is to say, he lives 20 metres away from the school, and he told me. When I saw him, he told me about it and said that the children were taken out of the school on one occasion and that they were lined up in the courtyard of his house and that, after that, they released them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you do not have any personal knowledge to the effect that the school had been surrounded by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not see anything personally, with my own eyes. However, I do have such knowledge, the source of which being a number of other people. So as I said, the school was surrounded by Serb soldiers. Whether members of the ex-JNA were also amongst them, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Who are these [redacted] that told you about that? Could you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us their names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted] [redacted]. I don't know his surname either. All three of them used to live at Vrace, so they were able to see personally what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You're saying that they were able to see personally what was going on. Do you know whether they could see that the police that was surrounded was divided into Serbs and Muslims and were they able to see that there was any conflict between the two of them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I note that the individuals whose names have been given by the witness were earlier described by him as being his friends and, therefore, those names may well tend to identify the witness. Might they be redacted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic. No objection? They will be redacted then.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the other hand, Mr. Ierace, the question is such it could have been objected to easily. I mean, if you ask for the names of the friends, of course. The problem you now demonstrated was visible already at that time. It would have saved us the specific procedure of redacting. So if you -- please, if you already from the question can find out that this might make the protective measures less effective, will you please object immediately next time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar, you will prepare the redaction. Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, would you please answer my question: Did your friends tell you, since they had told you that they had seen what was going on, did they also tell you that the school was separated into Serbs and Muslims and that there was conflict between the two sides?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is possible. However, I do not have any knowledge about that. I haven't heard of any such incident having taken place at the police school at Vrace.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Since in 1991 you were a member of the reserve police force, could you perhaps tell us who the Minister of the police was in 1991, 1992? The Minister of the police of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Minister of the police was Avdo ... the surname escapes me. Sorry. I'm sorry. The Minister of the police was Delimustafic, and his deputy was this person by the name of Avdo, and the second deputy Minister was Momcilo Mandic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1992, did you have an opportunity to see and have contact with these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: During 1992, I did have opportunity to see Momcilo Mandic; however, I didn't have any contact with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us where it was that you were able to see him? I'm referring to the neighbourhood of the town.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When was that? In 1991 or in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that you asked me whether I had the opportunity to see him during the war. There was no war in 1991, so I was referring to 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask you specifically about the war. I asked you about 1991 and 1992, because you were a member of the reserve police force and I wanted to know where and when you saw him, if you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that question asked by my friend is incorrect. The English translation of that question is: "I asked you about 1991 and 1992." But if one goes back to line 22, one sees that in fact she asked him specifically about 1992. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. On line 4 of page 16, the question was: "When was that? In 1991 or in 1992?" So later on it has been included. I don't think it creates great confusion, but perhaps could you please keep this in mind, Ms. Pilipovic, and then proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In 1992, did you have an opportunity to see Mr. Momo Mandic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When exactly in 1992 was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him on two or three occasions, so I couldn't tell you exactly when it was, but I'm sure that it took place in 1992. I remember that the first time I saw him it was in summertime, but I'm sure that I saw him again in the autumn.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see him before the war, that is, before April 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very often.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us when was the last time you saw him before April 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him in March, at the time the first barricades were set up.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you yourself have any knowledge about those barricades?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do have some knowledge about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What knowledge, when you say "some knowledge"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: At one point in time, I was able to -- I learnt who was on those barricades.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The people who were at the barricades, did they tell you where those barricades were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not necessary for them to tell me where they were. I could see them with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So where were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The barricades were set up at the junction near the School of Economics at the Bratstvo-Jedinstvo Bridge. One of the barricades was near the Vrbanja Bridge, next to the Unoninvest building, and one of them was opposite the Bratstvo-Jedinstvo Bridge, at the Pofalici neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you personally saw those barricades?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did; in particular, the ones at the Vrbanja and Bratstvo-Jedinstvo bridges.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you perhaps tell us when that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in March 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to the removal of those barricades? Were they removed at some point in time or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were removed several days later. Two days later, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know why they had been set up in the first place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were part of the measures, as a warning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Who set up those barricades as a warning, and a warning to whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The barricades were set up by the SDS, and they constituted a warning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object not only to this question, but to the line of questioning on the basis of relevance. We have had numerous questions as to the identity of the Minister for police, whether you ever saw him, even though you didn't have contact with him; who set up the barricades, how long they were up for, and so on. None of this material, in my respectful submission, is relevant to the evidence of the witness. In relation to credibility, one wonders - assuming that is the basis of the questioning - how this could be construed as a challenge to the witness's credibility. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, could you please explain to us what exactly on these issues you are now talking about, which, as far as I can see, has not been covered by the examination-in-chief, under what heading of Article 90(H) they're falling. Is this credibility? Is this testimony relevant to your case? And then please explain what your case is in this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. respect and tell it to the witness, as Rule 90(H)(ii) requires you to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. It is the position of the Defence that we may test the credibility of the witness in this manner, regardless of the fact that the questions were not raised during the examination-in-chief by my learned colleague. We should like to emphasise that, when giving the statement to the investigators of the Tribunal, the witness addressed these facts, the facts that have been raised by myself during the cross-examination. I'm talking about the facts relating to the incidents that happened in Sarajevo during the conflict or prior to the outbreak of the conflict. The Defence also wishes to emphasise that General Galic has been charged with having accepted the plan of siege of Sarajevo and the terror against civilians. It is the submission of the Defence that there were no such plans and that the issue or, rather, the case can be tested through the witnesses who at the time lived in Sarajevo. Therefore, my questions are relevant both for the credibility of the witness and the truthfulness of the witness's testimony, in view of the fact that he lived in Sarajevo at the relevant times and we were able to examine other witnesses to this effect as well. By doing so, it will be possible for us to test the credibility of the witnesses that have already been examined by the Prosecution and cross-examined by the Defence. So it is in this manner that we are testing the credibility of other witnesses as well. Let me also point out the fact - I'm not sure about the relevant transcript - that I objected to a question put by my learned colleague Mr. Blaxill to a witness he was examining at the time. The witness was being asked about the events which took place in April and May 1992, and you wanted me to explain my objection. The response of my learned colleague was that it was relevant for general allegations regarding the conflict on the territory of the city of Sarajevo. Likewise, it is our submission, Your Honour, that in view of the relevance of these questions, and as part of Rule 90(H)(ii), the Defence does have the right to cross-examine the witness about these allegations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. My friend says that the witness addressed these matters in his statement. Indeed, he did, but that alone is insufficient reason to cross-examine on these matters. The primary issue is always relevance. Secondly, my friend said that the accused is charged with having accepted the plan of siege of Sarajevo. That is incorrect. The accused is charged with having committed certain crimes against humanity, and the Prosecution has made plain in its pre-trial brief that the Prosecution maintains that the accused assumed control of a pre-existing campaign of sniping and shelling civilians. That has nothing to do with the so-called plan of siege of Sarajevo. Mr. President, I would have no objection to my friend cross-examining this witness about what occurred immediately prior to the time that the accused assumed control of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. These questions, however, well pre-date that period. Indeed, they pre-date the commencement of hostilities, and that is my objection, that that period is not relevant to the charges which the accused faces. Its relevance in this case can only be to generally set the scene. I emphasise what I have said in my opening and what has been said in the Prosecution pre-trial brief, that the Prosecution does not seek to place blame on one side or the other of the conflict. The Prosecution is not concerned with that. It's concerned purely and simply with crimes which it alleges the accused carried out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, would you please respond on this specific remark.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I hope that the time that my learned colleague and I are now using for this particular purpose -- first of all, I don't know how appropriate it is to discuss these matters in the presence of a witness, but I hope that this time is not going to be deducted from my cross-examination time. However, if you do not share my opinion, then we suggest that in respect of these matters which have also been brought up by my learned colleague, we convene a Status Conference so as not to lose time, and I think that in this manner we would be in a much better position to discuss the matters which are relevant; those matters which are relevant for the Defence and the matters which are relevant for the Prosecution. As for my response, the one that was forwarded to my learned friends from the Prosecution, the Defence claimed that there was no plan for terrorising the citizens of Sarajevo, that there was no order whatsoever that the civilian population of Sarajevo should be exposed to any form of terror, in particular that there was no pre-existing campaign before General Galic assumed his control as corps commander. The relevant times is -- are the year of 1992. As regards the issues that have now been raised concerning the month of April 1992, I will now finish the cross-examination of the witness who has provided answers to some of my questions. So with your permission, Your Honour, I should like to continue my cross-examination of the witness regarding the facts that are believed to be relevant and which were discussed during the examination-in-chief of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I'd first like to clarify a few things. First of all, cross-examining on the subject, as Rule 90(H) says, that is where it says: "Cross-examination shall be limited to the subject-matter of the evidence-in-chief." That is, the testimony given by the witness in court and not a statement previously given to investigators of the Prosecution. I think there was some misunderstanding about that. Then the second issue may be matters affecting the credibility of the witness. This is to be understood as the credibility of this witness, the credibility of this witness in relation to his testimony given in this court. Let me just give you an example. If we would ask who did win the Olympic Games on 10.000 metres speed skating, then of course this could be of some relevance, that it means that you can test the memory of the witness or -- so I wouldn't say that you cannot test the credibility of a witness on -- by using other subjects, but Rule 90(H) should be understood that credibility of the witness is credibility on those subjects touched upon in his testimony. And then, of course, we come to the last portion, that is, the witness, is he able to give evidence relevant to the case for the cross-examining party, to the subject matter of that case? I think at this moment we are dealing mainly with that. And although under 90(H)(ii) it says: "... counsel shall put to that witness the nature of the case of the party for whom that counsel appears which is in contradiction of the evidence given by the witness." This suggests already that the witness has given testimony which would undermine the Defence case. Then the Defence should put its case to the witness and then may examine the witness on these subjects. I think at this moment we are in this third section, the relevance to the case for the cross-examining party. And I do agree with you that especially since it is the case of the Defence that pre-existing -- a pre-existing campaign was not there, that you may ask questions on that subject to the witness. On the other hand, I noticed that the Prosecution has not specifically dealt with this issue during the examination-in-chief, but nevertheless, I will allow you, since this is a rather essential part of the case of the Defence, that you put some questions to him. I must say that, until now, the question whether this person, this Witness D, knew personally a minister or some other questions, it's not clear, to me at least, what would be the relevance of these questions and the answers given to these questions in respect to this part of the Defence case which is that there was no pre-existing campaign. If you please keep this in mind when you proceed, examine the witness. You have also heard that the Prosecution does not object in general against questioning in relation to the history of the conflict. That means the period immediately preceding the 6th of April. You may proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- for coming to my feet, but perhaps I should clarify what I said because, Mr. President, that is not my position. I did not object in general to questioning in relation to the period immediately before General Galic assumed command or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think I did say you did not object in general against questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: But the way that's come out in the transcript, and I think what you said, Mr. President, is that means the period immediately preceding the 6th of April. The 6th of April is approximately when the conflict commenced, and General Galic assumed command around the 10th of September, 1992. So my objection relates to cross-examination at length as to what happened before the 6th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. But if the accused has been charged with a pre-existing campaign, then of course if you want to establish that there was no pre-existing campaign, then of course it's -- you might go back as far as you want in order to demonstrate that there was no pre-existing campaign. So that's a bit difficult to limit it in time. Do you mean not pre-existing, not in June, not in May, not in April, not in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. March, not in January? So I will allow the Defence, to some extent, to look back in history to see whether there was a pre-existing campaign.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As you please, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you were born in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You lived all your life in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In which part of Sarajevo did you live?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the first two years of my life, I lived in Hrasno, and the rest of my life, I lived in Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So we can agree that the part of town that you lived in, you know it very well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know it well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us how many inhabitants, how many people live in Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer precisely how many people lived in Grbavica. I never had any access to official statistic as to how many people lived in Grbavica. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What was the ethnic composition of the population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was mixed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what was the dominant ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know about Grbavica, which the predominant ethnic group was; however, I do know that in the area of the municipality of Novo Sarajevo, to which Grbavica belongs, where I lived, the predominant or the majority population were Serbs. There were slightly more of them than Muslims, and there were not many Croats.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, during the examination-in-chief, you told us that a decision on mobilisation had been taken in Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know when that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was immediately after the arrival of the army in Grbavica, so this was early May, middle of May, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge whether before the decision was taken about the mobilisation in mid-May there was an earlier decision on mobilisation taken before that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about those decisions, but I know that many Serbs from Grbavica were already in the army when the front line was above Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was before -- in the first part of March, before the mobilisation. Before the mobilisation started, some of the Serbs were already in the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Where were they in the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the headquarters was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: According to what information do you claim that they were in the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because with these very same people I was in the army later myself, and I spoke to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What did they tell you when you spoke to them? Where were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: They told me they were in the army, on the front line, above Grbavica, where the front line was. That's where they were. Some of them told me that they had participated, that they had taken part and were at those barricades we spoke about earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, I would like to show the witness a map from the maps that I was given by my learned colleagues. With your permission, I would give the witness Map 1, which could be useful during the examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, in order to clarify, I think we have two exhibits. One is P3637, which is a map -- a set of five maps that were pre-marked but not marked -- no additional marks were made upon this map during the examination-in-chief. And then we also have Exhibit 3637D, which is a set of the same five maps, with some additional marks on it made during cross-examination. Which of the sets of maps of which you intend to show Map 1 are you using? The "D" version or the version P3637?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just P3637. It's a group of five maps that we got from my learned colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that no additional markings will be asked by you, because otherwise we would have to use the "D" version. You're just examining, not asking the witness to mark at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to have the witness indicate on the map where the positions or the front line was, since the witness spoke about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... witness to mark it on the map or not? I mean, that --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please use the "D" version, 3637D, because that is the copy we use for marking during examination-in-chief and cross-examination. Are the stickers on the map? Yes, they still are there. Okay. So we now have Map 1 of Exhibit 3637D on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, before you, you see a Map 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you indicate for us and mark it on the map where the front line was for which you said that was held by the soldiers who had told you that they had been to the front line. Which part of Grbavica is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: This line that I will indicate for you is the front line which I told you about that existed before Grbavica was taken. Is that what you want?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you just answer precisely whether this is the line that you had marked before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So according to you, these are positions where the army was, where the front line was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us: What do you believe is front? According to you, what is front? What is the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to me, I believe that the front line is the line along which the soldiers are positioned, whether they were trenches or their weaponry, or their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Considering that I can see that this line is located near your apartment or where your apartment used to be where you lived, could you answer whether in that area that you had marked, whether there were trenches along that line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Along that line there were trenches, and in the vicinity there was a bridge where a tank was located, and that tank was operated by a young man who was in -- he was doing his regular service in the JNA. I don't remember his name, but he comes from Milici.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us in this map -- could you mark for us other lines, other front lines that existed and were set up in Grbavica at the time, in the period before you volunteered in the army of Republika Srpska and until the moment that you left the army.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Do you mean the line of the front that was established after the taking of Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you, and I am asking you, to mark the front lines on Grbavica that existed during the time that you were there, that you lived there. Except that one line that you had marked, were there other front lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I would ask you to mark them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a front line that was set up when Grbavica was taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you answer who took Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was taken by the Serbian army, with the help of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the transcript, since we have been talking about marking at this moment, while the witness has just been pointing at pre-marked lines: The first marking, the first confrontation line, the witness pointed at a pre-marked black line somewhere in the middle between the words "Vrace" and "Kovacici," and the second so-called marking he pointed at the blue pre-marked line on Map 1. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you marked the position in relation to the street, in relation to Branka Surbeta Street. This is no longer the name of the street. So in relation to Vrace and in relation to Ozrenska Street, could you mark the lines, the front lines.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You could take a black biro and write it in. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The black, thick marking pen. Perhaps if you use dotted lines, then it becomes quite clear what has been marked at this moment. So if you mark the line asked by Ms. Pilipovic, then please mark it as a dotted line. Before you do so, could you please ask the question again, Ms. Pilipovic, what confrontation line to be marked or what -- how do you call it?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The front line in the area of Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The front lines in the area of Grbavica that were set up, according to the information of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Considering --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just trying to read your question again. Your question was: "So in relation to Vrace and in relation to Ozrenska Street, could you mark the lines, the front lines." Now, in rephrasing your question --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you're talking about Grbavica. Could you be quite precise on what you asked the witness to mark on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you and did you know -- do you know where the front line was and could you mark it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can mark it, but I would like to ask you to be precise as to what you want me to mark down. At one point, you know, you mentioned Vrace and Ozrenska and then you mentioned Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my question to the witness was very precise, to mark the front line towards Vrace, Vrace from the Branka Surbeta Street and from Ozrenska and Milinkladska Street. But perhaps the first question he could answer whether --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether that was the front line there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Branka Surbeta Street, there was no front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a front line in Dobojska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a front line in Ozrenska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark which part of Ozrenska Street was the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to mark it with a dotted line?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. D, may I interfere again? If you lean over too much to the map, the facial distortion may not be effective as it should be. So could you please try, as far as possible, to mark without leaning over too much? You don't have to sit -- it's a matter of not just going with your face quite so near the ELMO. I think the map should remain on the ELMO, but if you could just try to do it this way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry. I did not hear the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you lean over too much to the ELMO, then your facial distortion might not be complete. So would you please -- I wouldn't say lean back, but at least not go that much close to the ELMO while marking on the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask you whether I can mark the line on my desk and then put it back on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think if it would be possible to do it on the ELMO, then we are in a position to better see on -- how it is done. If you would just excuse me for one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do hear that the problems of the facial distortion do not exist any more, so do it just as it's convenient to you on the ELMO, please. Could the ELMO zoom out a bit so we can follow the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you marked a dotted line which went along Ozrenska Street and went down to Hrasno. That would be -- the front line would be Grbavica stadium and Milutina Djuraskovica Street, as far as I can see on this map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was -- the border was on the Milutina Djuraskovica Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell me, in Ozrenska Street, how far did the front line go, considering that you said that you were at that front line and that it went along the Ozrenska Street and the Milinkladska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The front line did not go Milinkladska Street. On that location where we were, the Milinkladska Street actually crosses with the Ozrenska Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you pass along the Ozrenska Street before the confrontation line was set up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In July when you were with the investigators, did you go to this street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see if this street continued after the intersection and went -- and went further on towards the Mojmilo hill? And this is no longer its name, Ozrenska. Do you know what its current name is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know. It's called Novopazarska Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether that street goes beyond this intersection as we look on the map towards Mojmilo? Yes, Mojmilo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: This marking "633," does this mean that this is -- is this an elevation point? Do you know what it means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know what that number means.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was that at this intersection the elevation of Gojino Brdo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that Gojino Brdo is slightly to the left of this number.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So we can agree that this marking -- that the marked Ozrenska Street does not stop at that intersection but it goes towards Mojmilo hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was at the front line, the street went further on. How far it went and how much further it went, I don't know. I was never there before the war and I never went after the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: While you were on the front line during the conflict, how far was Mojmilo hill away from the intersection here? You believe the Milinkladska-Ozrenska intersection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was some kind of hill. I don't know whether that was Mojmilo or part of Mojmilo or it was just the hill in the vicinity of the Mojmilo. But I believe that it was in this direction. To the left -- in any case, to the left there was Mojmilo hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Considering the front line of the Ozrenska Street and the location that you marked, this intersection, while you were on this line, in this position, were there any battles fought?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was there, there were -- there were no battles fought. While I was there, there was no combat. There were no battles. What I mean is there was no attempt to move the front lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How far away was the front line of the other side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know for sure, but certainly it wasn't very far away because it was a very populated settlement. There were -- and there were -- houses were very close by. So there was not a far distance whether we look from below or from above. It was not possible to see very far away.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark on this map, in relation to the Ozrenska Street, where was the position of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would ask you to repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to the Ozrenska Street where you marked the front line, could you mark the front line of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot mark it because I was never at that front line. But I believe that it was in the immediate vicinity of this front line. Simply it went parallel with this line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When we look at this map, was this -- their line down below towards the Grbavica stadium. And when we look Milinkladska Street -- from the Milinkladska Street, was perhaps from that front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Milinkladska Street, as I told you already, was not a front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you in relation to Ozrenska Street. When we look at the map towards the Grbavica stadium, along which streets was the front line or could you please mark it for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The front line was just below Ozrenska Street, in that part where I was, you see. And as you go towards the Grbavica stadium, then it goes further and further below Ozrenska Street. So it went down until up to the Grbavica stadium. And then it went on further Milutina Djuraskovica Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark it for us. Could you please mark these positions on the street.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already done so.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to Milutina Djuraskovica Street and down Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Going by the Grbavica stadium and in relation to Milutina Djuraskovica Street. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The front line was along the street of Milutina Djuraskovica.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that below the Grbavica stadium there was a front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "below" or "under."

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Where it says in front of "Hrasno" "Brace Ribar," I believe this is a boulevard. It says "Dinarska." The intersection of Milutina Djuraskovica Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is where the front line went, where the Dinarska Street and the Milutina Djuraskovica Street cross.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Does this front line go to the left in relation to Brace Ribar Street or does it go to the right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can see as you go down by the Grbavica stadium and you come to the Dinarska Street, then the front line goes to the left and then it goes straight on towards the Miljacka River.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Considering that you were there for -- for -- there for more than a year at the front line in Lenjinova Street and you marked that line, do you have any knowledge in relation to the Omladinsko Setaliste, whether the front line went to the right or to the left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you -- if we're facing the Omladinsko Setaliste, the front line from that position, which I marked in blue line on the map, the front line went both to the left and to the right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to this front line that you were at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And it says Omladinsko Setaliste. How far in relation to this front line was the front line of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did this line go further along the Omladinsko Setaliste towards Hrasno?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is regarding the front line of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you tell me what kind of marking should I make?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: With a blue marker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you have to use a black marker anyhow. You have got a black marker?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With a dotted line or a full line?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Dotted line. In fact, why don't you do a full line, considering these were the BH army positions, so that then we have the dotted line used for the positions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. D, if this is the -- if these are the positions of the BiH army, please use a full line and not a dotted line. So now you can make a full line. That's what is suggested by you, Ms. Pilipovic, and I think what the witness didn't actually do. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks] I apologise, but when I was marking the Serb army positions, I made a mistake. I can see that now.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If you could, could you draw the positions of the Serb army in a dotted line and then --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the Serb army positions. That's why I used a dotted line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now draw in the positions of the BH army, please, with a full line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that along this line, both lines, that the distance between the two front lines, according to you, was very small? And could you tell us approximately how much it is expressed in metres or kilometres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: At some points it was a small distance; at others, it was a large distance. For example, at the Grbavica stadium, it was rather large.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How large?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the breadth of a stadium.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And what about towards -- in relation to Omladinsko Setaliste and Ozrenska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've already said. With respect to Omladinsko Street, it is 150 metres, approximately, whereas is Ozrenska, their positions in Ozrenska, I was never able to see, actually, but I can assume that the distance was quite small, 50-odd metres perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me when I say that in respect to the line, this part of town was divided between the Serb army and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, or the army of Republika Srpska and the BH army, after these lines were established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the confrontation line, the demarcation line between the army of Republika Srpska and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When did you go to the front line for the first time when you volunteered for the army of Republika Srpska in June 1992? When did you go first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: That same evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, we are close to a quarter to 11.00. You might have noticed that we went on a bit longer than usual. That's because we'll stop at 1.00. So we'll adjourn for half an hour and just have one break. Could you please find a suitable moment within the next one or two minutes to interrupt your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a good place to take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So we'll have one break this morning. We'll adjourn until a quarter past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, that evening when you went to your positions, how many of you were there, or were you alone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were more of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How many of you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole platoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you were all together at the place where your headquarters was; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you be more specific and tell us what location that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the place where the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please put off your microphone, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the place where a company called Drvo Rijeka was located before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, apart from the rifle which you said you kept, you were issued, were you issued a uniform as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not issued a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What about the other members of your platoon? What were they wearing? Did they have uniforms or were they without uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them had a complete uniform set, the kind that the former JNA wore. Others had parts of uniforms. Some wore boots, others had trainers, sports shoes. People were dressed differently.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Who issued the order for you to take up your positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The leader of the platoon, [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have a department [as interpreted] within your platoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you didn't have a leader for the squad.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What orders did you receive from the platoon commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was that we were to take up our positions, and he said who was to be deployed where. He would call out our names and say, "So-and-so to take up that position," another person to take up another position, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Line 41 -- that is page 41, line 11 of the English transcript reads: "Q. Did you have a department within your platoon?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: "A." - answer - "No." And I think it was translated in the same form in terms of the voice. That question, to me, does not make sense. I assume that there is a mistranslation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter I apologises. It was "squad."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So your squad commander told you what positions you would be taking up; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did the platoon commander issue any orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Which?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said -- he ordered us to be very careful, to be cautious, and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to open fire as soon as we saw something.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In your platoon, were you able to open fire without the commander giving orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which are you -- which commander are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Referring to the leader of your platoon. You said that he was the one to issue orders.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I could decide myself when to open fire and when not to open fire, and his orders were general orders that we should fire on time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So when could you open fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was able to open fire when I saw fit, when I thought it was necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you in fact open fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I wanted to.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you inform your commander that you fired when you thought you should do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because he was informed about that, so there was no need to inform him separately about that. He already knew that we opened fire when we considered it necessary to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: While you were at those positions, did the other side fire at you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, except sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I just wanted to remind you about the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: While you were on duty, did the snipers target you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at all the positions that were visible, that the snipers on the other side could see and target.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: From your position, could you see the facilities or parts of town that the snipers were firing from? I'm talking about the Muslim side, from the Muslim side.
