utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you show us on the map in relation to the front line and your position there? Could you mark the buildings and tell us which they were from which the snipers fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I place an "X" at that point?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can put an "X," and tell us what the building or location was called.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. I shall mark in an "X" and tell you what the place was called. This building was the building of the Executive Council.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you make any additional markings, would you please add a "1" to this "X" or use other letters when marking other locations. So either add a "1" or use -- for the next location you will mark a "Y" or a "Z" or a "W."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I put an "X2" at this other place?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This building was the Mathematics Faculty, Natural Sciences and Mathematics Faculty building.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was the Machine Engineering Faculty building close by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Machine Engineering building was right next door to the Natural Sciences and Maths Faculty.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark that building for us? And was there a sniper firing from that building too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a sniper, but the sniper did not target our positions. Our positions were not clearly visible from that building.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was the building of the Electricity Board there too, the Electroprivreda building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a little lower down on the map and towards the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark that on the map, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the electricity building?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to put an "X3" there?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is the Bristol Hotel close by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether there was a sniper on top of the hotel? And if so, would you mark it in, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had heard that there was a sniper shooting from that building too.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Then could you mark in the position of the Bristol Hotel.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What about the Unoninvest [phoen] building? Is it located there too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: While you were at your position, did any shooting come from that side and from those positions? Was there any sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I've already said, from the Executive Council building and the Natural Sciences and Mathematics Faculty building.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether, on the side that your positions were, anybody was killed by sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know something about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What about the members of your platoon? Were any of them wounded or killed by sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nobody from my platoon was killed by sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: But you know that some people were killed. Were they civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were civilians too.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The time you spent at those positions, do you happen to know how many civilians were killed while you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about three civilians who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: While you were on duty - and you said you worked in shifts - did your shift have to report about the daily events during your shift? Did you have to make a report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not have to make any special reports. But as I have already said, we did have a telephone communication line with the headquarters in Drvo Rijeka, so we were able to communicate by phone.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether your platoon commander wrote reports on the activities of his men and the situation up at the front line covered by your platoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he did. I think he reported via the company commanders to the headquarters in Banjalucka Street, because I know they went to the headquarters in Banjalucka Street for consultations. There were also situations where the battalion commander would tour the front line and things of that kind. And that's how I'm able to conclude that they did have constant contact, that they knew what was going on at the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that your platoon commander's reports to the company commander, do you happen to know whether they were oral reports or written reports?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he reported orally or in written form. I think that previously they had been oral reports, but I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you yourself, in view of your position, if you noted any irregularities in the course of your shift at the front line, would you inform your superior officer, the platoon commander, telling him that this was not in line with war -- the laws of war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never informed him about things like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The members of your platoon or the members of the company, do you happen to know whether any of them was wounded during the fighting or were their lives in jeopardy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some of them were wounded, and some of them were killed too.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: While you were at those positions, there was armed conflict. There was fighting on both sides.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, at Grbavica, which I marked in in the map, there was no fighting except this sniper fire. And this also applies to the Ozrenska Street positions while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did the snipers respond, the ones you saw on the high-rise buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand your question. Could you explain what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the snipers who were positioned on the high-rise buildings at your positions, did they fire at the opposite side, and if so, in which direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that they did open fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that they were positioned on those high-rise buildings as snipers to retaliate and respond to the fire incoming from the top of the Executive Council building and the Mathematics Faculty building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with you there because I know that that wasn't the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that while you were at the front line at Ozrenska Street, that there was no shooting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was there, there was no -- the lines did not move. There were no heavy conflicts. But a sniper did shoot quite frequently on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us how long the front line was in Ozrenska Street and also the front line where your position was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The front line at Ozrenska Street is a very long line, whereas my platoon's line was about 150 metres long. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So the line at Ozrenska Street was longer than 150 metres; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to know how many people were positioned at the front line in Ozrenska Street?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting. I think there's a problem with the transcript, commencing -- I would take it first at page 48, line 1:

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that while you were at the front line at Ozrenska Street, that there was no shooting." That question does not accurately reflect the evidence. I suspect there may be a translation problem rather than my friend -- my learned friend improperly putting a question. And then in the answer at line 4 of page 48, this appears: "A. But a sniper did shoot quite frequently on both sides." I'd be surprised if the witness said "a sniper." I would expect it was, rather: "But sniping or snipers did shoot quite frequently on both sides," having regard to the clear evidence so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think in the answer the witness corrected already some of the objections you made against the question as such. But could you please, Ms. Pilipovic, clarify the issue about the shooting, whether there was sniping fire or there was a sniper? In -- your question was that -- you said: "While you were at the front line at Ozrenska Street, there was no shooting." I think the testimony was that there was sniper fire. So that is an incorrect statement if it's well translated. So would you please clarify this issue on whether -- yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question was whether there was any armed combat, armed operations while he was up at the front line at Ozrenska Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would this mean that you made no reference at all to the testimony earlier given by the -- I mean, the question was introduced by quoting or at least referring to the testimony of the witness. Would you please rephrase that question again, where exactly, and also try to clarify on whether there was one sniper or sniping fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question was whether at the front lines where the witness was positioned while he was a member of the army of Republika Srpska, which was the front line in Lenjinova Street and Ozrenska Street, whether there was any armed operations or, rather, was there shooting from both sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, your question at page 48, line 1, starts with referring to the statement of the witness. Is this an incorrect translation or did you refer to the statement of the witness? I'm not talking about your question that followed but the reference to the -- to the testimony of the witness. It reads in English: "Q. You said that while you were at the front line at Ozrenska Street, that there was no shooting." That's what the translation says. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my question was as follows -- it wasn't shooting. What I said was armed operations, and I was referring to what the witness said. While he was up at the front line in Ozrenska Street, there were no armed operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then there might be a problem as far as the translation is concerned. Would you please then clarify the issue of "sniping fire" or "a sniper" by putting this question to the witness more specifically.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any sniping at the front lines in Ozrenska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was sniping at the front lines in Ozrenska Street, coming from both sides, on both sides. And if I may, what you were discussing a moment ago, may I clarify something to avoid misunderstanding? May I clarify what we discussed a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: While you were in Ozrenska Street, at the positions there, you said that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the witness asked whether he could clarify an issue, and I would like to give him the opportunity to clarify, because he -- it aims at avoiding misunderstandings. Mr. D, you may clarify the answer given.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were armed operations at Ozrenska, and I said that there was sniping from both sides. And I'm talking about the time period when I was present there. Fire from the other side was not opened except for the sniping. While we were there, we did open fire, from all the weapons that we had in our possession at the time. I'm talking about the time I was there, the periods I spent there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We're now talking about Ozrenska Street. What weapons did you possess, did your battalion - I'm sorry, your platoon - possess while you were at these positions at Ozrenska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had all types of infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell us about these infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: In most of the cases, it consisted of an automatic rifle, 7.62 millimetres, that is, a semi-automatic rifle; then a machine-gun, 7.62 millimetres. Available to us was also a weapon which is used for launching grenades, the so-called Zolja, which is a hand-held rocket launcher. Furthermore, we had weapons for directional fire, anti-personnel weapon, which is activated with a trigger. We had sufficient amount of ammunition. We also had two kinds of anti-personnel grenades, two machine-guns of an older type, 7.92 millimetres calibre. There were no sniping rifles in my platoon. No one was issued with a sniping rifle or an M-84 machine-gun in my platoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Out of the weapons that you have now indicated, what was in the possession of your platoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything except for sniping rifles and M-84 machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So there was a person in charge of a mortar in your platoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: A mortar is something different. I was talking about hand-held rocket launchers, about Zoljas. This is a different type of weapon that you actually carry on your shoulder when firing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In Ozrenska Street, while you were on duty on your position, was there a mortar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was, but it was not operated by the people from my platoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So while you were there on the position, since you stated that there was no activity, such activity, you did not use a mortar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that there was no combat activity at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I appreciate the witness has clarified that problem in relation to combat activity, but I would be grateful if my friend would not put to the witness inaccurately his previous testimony. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I think there is at least some reason for that, unless there is a translation problem. But could you please try, as I stress again and again, to quote as precisely as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness enumerated the weapons which, according to his knowledge, were used while he was on position in Ozrenska Street. I am only concerned about the accurate translation of the so-called Zolja, the weapon which the witness said was issued to the members of his platoon while he was in Ozrenska Street, and that was the reason why I asked whether they had a mortar as well. I wanted to clarify to avoid any mistakes in interpretation, because so far the witness did state that there was a mortar in Ozrenska Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't mind your line of questioning. I just remind you on referring to testimony given before as precisely as possible. That was not always done. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, while you were deployed on the positions in Ozrenska Street, who manned the mortar which was positioned there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some soldiers who were not members of my platoon or my company.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know what unit they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean which company they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Which formation or unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were members of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You learned about that particular fact, that they were members of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, from them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The individuals in question were local residents, so it was only logical that they should be members of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. They were people who used to live there before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you that they were members of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, or was it your conclusion because of the fact that they were local residents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never explicitly asked them whether they were members of the Sarajevo Corps, so they could not have provided me with such an answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you came to that conclusion on the basis of the fact that they lived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: They lived there, and it was obvious that their activity, mortar activity, was consistent with our activity. They made sure that it was consistent with our activity.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of mortar was it, the one that you were able to see? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't exactly remember the calibre, so I'm not in a position to tell you. I don't remember that. All I can tell you is that it was a medium-calibre barrel. As far as I know, there were three types of calibre, and this one, I think, was of medium calibre.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the number of the members of the mortar crew was, in view of the military regulations? What would have been the number of the crew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is there a gunner who is a part of that mortar crew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a so-called gunner as part of the mortar crew, who is in charge of moving the barrel and adjusting the target in accordance with what they want to fire at.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were you present when they fired this mortar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not present. I was not able to see it with my own eyes. However, the placement was some 30 metres away from our positions, so I was able to conclude from the sound of the detonation that the firing was done from there, from that placement.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the map which is in front of you, could you please indicate for us and show us where the Jewish cemetery is located.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could do that. [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark the location with a circle so as to differentiate it from other markings.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to your positions and facing the Jewish cemetery, could you indicate for us where the front line was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to your positions and facing the Jewish cemetery, could you indicate for us where the front line was, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean where the front line at the Jewish cemetery was? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, just for the sake of clarity, could you please indicate at what time you want to have the front line indicated by the witness since the testimony was before that there have been changes from the beginning of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was referring to the period while the witness was a member of the VRS until his departure from that force. That is, June 1992 until May 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness D, could you please mark for us where the front line was during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I can be very specific and precise, because I was never present on that front line. However, I do have an idea where it was so I can approximate.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you do that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would be the location of the line, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: While you were a member of this platoon, did your commander ever tell you and your colleagues that there was an order issued by the Presidency of the Republika Srpska concerning the respect of regulations and laws of war, and were you at any point in time warned to that effect, that is, that you should abide by those provisions while you were on duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were never warned to that effect. We never received any such instruction.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: While you were a member of this platoon, were you aware of the battalion or the brigade to which your platoon was subordinated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know what brigade our platoon belonged to. I did not have information about that structure and the hierarchy of those military units. I must say that I was not interested in knowing about this hierarchy.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the corps command was? That is, the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, do you know where it was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us who wrote the authorisations that you received when -- prior to your leaving the territory.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received the first authorisation at the Drvo Rijeka headquarters. The second one, I had to go to the Banjalucka Street to get it, and it was signed in my presence by the deputy commander, [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As regards the authorisations that you provided to the OTP and which were subsequently disclosed to the Defence, it says that in October you were authorised to travel to Ruma and Sombor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not go to Sombor.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you travel to Ruma?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As regards the second authorisation with the destination Belgrade, did you actually travel to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Why did you go to Ruma?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I travelled to Ruma because my friends live there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you had left the VRS after you received the second authorisation in the month of May.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Why is it that you decided never to return?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I didn't want to get killed and because I wanted to become reunited with my family.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that your family was not with you at Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of my family was and part of it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were your parents with you at Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What about the other part of your family? Who do you have in mind when you say the other part of the family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did your brother live in Ruma or Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What about your daughter? Where did she live?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President, firstly on the grounds of relevance, and secondly because the answer may tend to identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you respond, Ms. Pilipovic, on both aspects of the objection. And please keep in mind also that, during the response, we should respect the -- the protective measures that are existing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, where exactly at Grbavica did you live?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I lived at Grbavica in the [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In which street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that on the 22nd of June, you had moved with your parents to [redacted]-- I don't need to mention the name of the street. I think you understand which street I have in mind.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did your family move with you to [redacted], that is, your parents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who do you have in mind when you speak about my family?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, if you say that you don't have to name the street, I'm a bit surprised that you do just one moment afterwards. I suggest that already -- although the Prosecution has not objected, I'd like to have redacted the -- any detail about where Witness D lived, what street, what area. We know that he has been living in Grbavica and that's, I think for the time being, good enough. Madam Registrar, would you please prepare the redaction. And please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence is in the possession of a statement which was given by the witness to the OTP investigators in 1997. I merely wish to check whether the allegations made in the statement by the witness are correct. The witness stated on page 1 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- page 2, actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, let me interrupt you. If this can be done without violation of the protective measures that have been granted later on [sic], fine. If not, you should make a proposal to do it otherwise. So I do understand what your intention is, but the means how to come to your aim are still bound by the protective measures. So either you can do it without violating them, then please proceed. If not, you can make any suggestion to have this clarified in any other way with full respect of the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence should like to suggest that the first page of the statement given by the witness to the OTP investigators, 00969512 in the B/C/S version, be submitted to the witness. And we propose that the witness reads this page of his statement, and then I should like to ask him to confirm, by simply nodding his head, whether the contents of the statement are correct, and in that way I think we will not identify him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I'm asking, Your Honour, is for the witness to say, "Yes, that's correct," or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You also suggested that he would read this statement first, and then, of course, nodding your head is of a neutrality which is not of great help to solve the problem. I would suggest that you confer -- I don't know how much time you will still use for the cross-examination. If it would be finished before 1.00, I would suggest that you confer with the Prosecution and to communicate what line you would like to show to the witness, and then he doesn't have to read it. And then I think this part of the statement can be tendered into evidence and then, of course, sealed. So that it is not necessary to read it, that the Chamber can read it at the moment it is tendered, and the protective measures are fully respected. So that would be my suggestion, and not to have this part of the statement read by the witness and the subsequent nodding yes or no. Would that -- is there any objection from the Prosecution in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I would simply add that I have no objection to the witness reading the relevant part to himself and then confirming the accuracy of the relevant part. Secondly, having regard to my learned friend saying earlier that the material is in statement form, I would simply seek to respectfully remind the Defence that there is still current an order made by the pre-trial Chamber in June of 2000 forbidding -- directing that statements and the like are not to be disclosed publicly. Effectively, the order limits the communication of the contents of witness statements to that which occurs between Defence counsel and the accused. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic, what do you think about my suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Your Honour, I accept your proposal. I think that it will be sufficient for my colleagues to see which page of the statement I'm talking about, and then later on, we will tender that page into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I think that will not be enough, because the Chamber has to know exactly what the witness was asked to read. I mean, otherwise we get a full page and we don't know what part the witness was confronted with. So I don't know. If you do not -- I don't know whether you'll conclude your cross-examination before 1.00. If not, please prepare a copy of that page, show it to the Prosecution, indicate clearly on that page what lines you're asking the witness to confirm, so that the Chamber also knows later on, if it has been admitted into evidence, although sealed, that we know, at least, what it is all about. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness D, you testified that while deployed in Ozrenska Street, that the front line was rather long. Were any trenches located there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How many days per week would you remain deployed on those positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was deployed there six or seven times, and each time we would stay for five days without any interruption, apart from the last time I was there, when we stayed only one day.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you receive food while on duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: There, at the very location.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any kitchen which was in charge of supplying food to the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The food was brought to us in a house just above Ozrenska Street, and it was from that house that it was distributed to the soldiers on the line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: While you were a member of the VRS, you told us that there were casualties and fatalities amongst soldiers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the wounded soldiers were being treated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Initially it was in Tilave [phoen], apart from severe cases that were transported to the hospital in Pale. When this war hospital was no longer there in Tilave, then the soldiers were transported to the barracks. There was an infirmary at Vrace.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Colonel Toni Posa was treating soldiers at Tilave hospital, him being a Slovenian and a member of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that members of other ethnic groups were amongst the corps personnel, except for Slovenians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know only of this individual.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of Lieutenant Colonel Skolar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You're not aware of the fact that he was a Slovenian and a member of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just need to consult my colleague. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: While you were at the position in Lenjinova Street, you were deployed in skyscrapers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next to the skyscrapers.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What was the disposition? How many soldiers were deployed at these positions by the -- next to the skyscraper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the first skyscraper, there were three; second, there were two or three; and at the third one, sometimes there were two soldiers, sometimes three, it depended on how many soldiers were available. And on the fourth one, there were always four soldiers available.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the period while you were at those positions, were there people living in those skyscrapers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there were also many flats that had been abandoned.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were these buildings damaged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The fourth skyscraper, its top had burnt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, just in order to have a look at the clock, as you know, I reminded the Prosecution as well several times that we are taking a lot of time. You just asked the witness about the number of members of his platoon employed at the different buildings. This has been asked by the Prosecution, and in full detail, and the witness gave exactly the same answer. So it's purely repetitious, but I waited to make this comment until the moment that you continued, because there was no subsequent question testing the credibility. You just accepted the answer as it was given and continued on other issues. So would you please either explain to us now what was the reason for repeating this question or -- yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I will explain.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I missed asking the question whether, according to your knowledge, since you were a member of the platoon, these numbers were sufficient to cover this front line where the skyscrapers were located?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You could have asked this without repeating the question about the numbers. You could just indicate, "Yesterday you gave exact numbers, two or three or four at each building," would have been enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you answer this question, please? In the way that you were positioned, was there enough of you to cover the front line from possible firing or armed operations, the positions that is the skyscrapers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not a military expert, and I cannot make this kind of assessment.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. I will now allow my colleague to take over the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would there be any indication as far as the time you would use, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you so much, Mr. President. I am not going to go on for very long. Possibly a quarter of an hour unless there is an interruption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hello, sir. I would also like to ask you some questions. My first question: You said -- you told us about your professional qualifications, and you said that you were not able to work, but you did not tell us whether you were receiving your salary during the period in question. Were you receiving a salary during the period in question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to the question as it presently reads. I'd ask that my learned friend clarify the question. Is he referring to the period of time that the witness was a member of the platoon? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please. Could you make it more precise Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. period -- I'm talking about the period, more precisely, when the witness, before he became a member of the Serbian army, when he was living in Grbavica and said that he was not able to work for geographical and political reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in that case, I object on the grounds of relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please indicate what the relevance is, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is very relevant, Mr. President. It is a very relevant question, because I believe that Mr. Ierace understood it very well, that this answer will justify the relevance of the first question that goes to the credibility of the witness, because this witness engaged himself voluntarily in an army that he left in an irregular manner. So my second question would be whether he was paid by -- if he was receiving a salary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... received any salary for his military activities or for his civilian activities he was not able to perform?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. What I want to know is, firstly, Mr. President, whether he received or not his salary before he volunteered for the army; and secondly, whether he received a salary after he became a member.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness D, did you understand the questions? Could you please then answer these questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is not clear enough. I don't understand what is meant when "salary" is mentioned, whether they mean the salary for my civilian activity or for my military activity. Could somebody explain this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will put a question to you. The first question is: When you were not able to work, not as a military but before, as a civilian, did you receive your salary of your employer, if employed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I did not receive a salary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you receive a salary when you were still at work? So before the situation existed that you were not able to go to work.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the next question is whether you received any salary for your military activities when you had joined your platoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if there are any additional questions, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. This is exactly where I wanted to arrive at. Sorry, I was interrupted by the Prosecution, so I'll be a little longer. But the second question I'd like to ask the witness is the following, and I would like to get a yes or no answer, if that is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So I am considering that you entered an army, you became a member of the army voluntarily that -- an army was going to pay you a salary. Is that correct? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "regular," because I was not mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What I said was "voluntarily."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't understand what you mean I was a regular member of the army. What do you mean "regular"? Could you please explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Okay. Voluntarily. Voluntarily. You have already indicated this, that you had a contract. It was your own decision. This was your proprio motu. It was your own will. Of your own free will you entered, you became a member of an army.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes. I became a member of the army voluntarily, and I was a regular soldier of the VRS, of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So -- and I believe that you became a member voluntarily for the motives -- for personal motives.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Sir, after you decided -- when you decided to leave the army, is it true to say that you acted as a deserter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I became a member of the army voluntarily under a great psychological pressure, and I left the army as a deserter under a great psychological pressure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: As a deserter, yes. It is the answer to my question. I would like to ask another question. At the moment, sir, that you decided to leave this army that you by yourself joined, your parents, were they still living in Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, you declared during your testimonial that when you entered, when you became a member of the army, it was your fear for your family, primarily for your parents, and it was -- in the light of this testimony, isn't there a contradiction if you are deserting at the time when your parents are still residing in Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You know, a war -- a war is full of contradictions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your answer. You have told us, sir, that you were not wearing a uniform when you were active in your unit. Could I then believe that on the other side there were also combatants - and I'm insisting on this term "combatant" - who on the front line were also not wearing a uniform, on the other side?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President. The question does not at this stage correctly reflect the witness's evidence. The question in part states, "You have told us, sir, that you were not wearing a uniform when you were active in your unit." That appears to reflect the answers given to questions asked by Ms. Pilipovic. In fact, he was asked whether he was issued with a uniform when he first joined the platoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand your objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you first clarify the issue on whether the witness has not -- did not wear a uniform during the whole period of his military activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my question wasn't exactly such. On page 41, I believe 18:05 - I can perhaps take up the transcript on that stage - I heard the witness say that he did not receive a uniform. That means he was not issued with a uniform. That means that he was -- had sports shoes, jeans. So he was without uniform. He did not wear a uniform. During the same period --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the question was aiming at the period when he first went to his platoon, so that does not clarify whether he had not a uniform during the whole period of his activity. But you are referring to the testimony - let me just try to find it - that, "You were not wearing a uniform when you were active in your unit." That's the English translation. And that would cover the whole period of time. While the answer given by the witness, as far as my recollection goes, was about whether he was issued a uniform at the time when he was sent to his platoon first. Additional questions then were what the other members of his platoon were wearing. So would you please, if you want to continue this question, either rephrase your question thus that it does not cover the whole period of his military activity or --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or first ask this question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, at the time -- and this is referring to your first statement at the period when you joined the army. You said -- you testified that you were not issued a uniform. So my question is the following: Is it true to say that at the same time that we -- it is true to say that at the same time, on the other side, there were combatants, soldiers who were not in uniform, who were not wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who do you mean from "the other side"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, you said yourself that there were combatants on one side. This is the terms that you used yourself when we are talking about the other side. So we are talking about the enemy. So independent of their race or religion. So the other side.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea what they were wearing. I never saw them. My only occasion to see them was on TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, are you saying to me that you never saw combatants while you were at the front line, no matter who they were? You were frightened of being killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's exactly what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to return to the incidents mentioned by this witness. I would like to have a specific answer to something, and I'm thinking about the mortar shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You said that you saw soldiers who were drunk and who were firing, who were firing a mortar or mortars in this area that you marked on a photograph. And the photograph is P3252, and you identified it yourself. Now, as I'm referring to this photograph, I would like to ask you the following question: Firstly, could you tell us the name of the street which is located --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we could again from the photograph on the -- put the photograph on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please finish your question, because you started a question without finishing it. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please put on the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. President. I would like to -- if it is possible to have first -- that's what I was waiting for, for the photograph to be put on the ELMO, and that was not appearing on the screens, so that I could ask the question and then refer to the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't hear you finish your question, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to finish my question with the photo on the screen. The photo is on the screen, but I don't see it on my screen. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I apologise. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, so we are looking at the street at the back, the back of the photograph. Could you tell us what the name of the street is? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It is Radnicka Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What is the name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radnicka Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the item -- or what is the view that we have from the circle that you have marked on the other side, on the right-hand side of the photograph, more specifically, on the other side of the street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the circle marked on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: From the circle, from the circle that's marked on the photograph - and we're looking on the right-hand side of the photograph, so on the other side of the street - in which direction are we looking? If you can indicate it for me, and if you can't, then could you please say so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry. I don't understand the question at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm going to rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... more clear. Do you expect an answer like north, west, south, east, or city or hills or --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is impossible for me to determine north, south, east, or west. What I would like to know is the direction of firing, since we were told that there were mortars located there. So I would like to -- this is the answer that I want to get out of this witness. So we're looking -- we don't even know where the mortars were firing at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please answer the question, Mr. D.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mortars were located in such a way that the mortars were fired from the south to the north. The shells were fired from ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If you say "from the south to the north," what was the target?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean what the shells were targeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: The city was targeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the question follows, sir: You, as a lawyer, as a graduate of law, for what reason, after you have seen this people who were drunk operating a mortar, why didn't you inform your superiors of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Considering my ethnicity, I would absolutely not dare do such a thing. If I was a Serbian, of Serbian ethnicity, this would have had no effect whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Sir, the last question: You said that you were given an order to fire, and I believe that this is what the English text says, at anything that moved. Did you at the time protest to your superiors about this order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not, and none of my colleagues did either.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Last -- honestly, last question: You said, sir, line 17, page 1890, that there were camps of forced labour that inhabitants of the city could be taken to. At the time, did you yourself see one or several of these camps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see these camps. I heard about these camps from the testimonies of people who were in those camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. No more questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Before giving the opportunity to the Prosecution to re-examine the witness, I just first want to know whether one of my colleagues has any additional questions. Yes, please, Judge Elmahdi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ELMAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you said that you never reported to your superiors once you finished your daily shift or a shift of several days. The ammunition that was given to you, was it not checked out? That is to say, did they not know that you used some ammunition if you fired, or wasn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were able to hear it and they were able to know about it, because when we ran out of ammunition, we would ask for fresh ammunition to be given us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ELMAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Without asking what you shot at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't ask, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have some additional questions as well, Mr. D. I think you told us - when I'm not correct, please tell me - that you knew about three civilians killed by snipers, I think you said. These three, these casualties, you knew them personally, or is this the information you've got about all the casualties among civilians caused by sniping fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two of the civilians I knew personally, whereas the third civilian was the mother of an acquaintance of mine, but I never actually met her. I didn't know her personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know of any number of casualties among civilians other than from these three, other than these three?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were more, but I couldn't give you an exact figure. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My next question is whether you know anything about civilians on a regular basis being targeted by sniping fire, civilians living on your side of the front line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was shooting often.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My next question is the following: You testified that you never reported any irregularities, if you noticed them, irregularities in the sense that colleagues of yours would behave against the laws of the war. My first question is: Did you ever notice such irregularities? I clarify myself. "Not reporting" can mean two things: you didn't notice them or you noticed them but you did not report them. Could you please clarify your answer that you gave before.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: First let me say that I did see many irregularities, and I can bear that out by giving -- quoting concrete examples. In one particular situation, when civilians were being evicted from Grbavica, I talked to one of my fellow platoon members as to what was going on, and he agreed to go to the headquarters of the military police to ask for an explanation why this was being done, but he didn't receive an answer. On another occasion, I went to the military police to seek protection for a civilian in the building where I lived, and they were going to take him away sometime towards evening. Anyway, I went there and found a military policeman on duty and told him what I was about, and he asked me who the person in question was, who the man was, and I said it was a Muslim. And he just waved his hand, waved it aside. But I didn't inform my commanders or the military or civilian police about any other irregularities. It did no good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My next question is: Do you have knowledge of the laws of the war, and in what detail, if you have any knowledge of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have any detailed knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. My next question is: You have been -- you have testified that on - I just have to find the name of the street again - on Ozrenska Street you had all different kinds of weaponry with you, and among this weaponry, for example, rocket launchers. You told us that you fired, at least your platoon fired, with this weaponry. Could you tell us what the targets were and at what situations you would fire this weaponry. You mentioned a couple of different weapons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: This type of weaponry, the Zolja type of hand-held rocket launcher, I never had occasion to use. My colleagues used it to target the houses which were below us when they suspected that there was somebody there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just add a question: "Houses when someone was there," do you mean that there was any military presence or that the mere presence of even civilians would be sufficient?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anybody's presence would be sufficient to warrant this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And houses at approximately what distance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: They weren't far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you mean near to the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your answers. Is there any need for re-examining the witness? Please, Mr. Ierace, proceed. We'll stop at 1.00, so if by working very efficiently it could be achieved by then, it would be fine; if not, we'll see.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, you've been asked a number of questions by both the Defence and Their Honours as to why it was that you did not complain about irregularities. You've given evidence that you were present when Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. civilians on the other side of the confrontation line were, in your opinion, deliberately shot. You've given evidence that, as I understand it, that on all of those occasions, the civilians were shot by members of the sniping unit. Firstly, am I correct in that summary of your evidence so far?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Mr. President, I have an objection to make. I think it was stated in the text that instructions, orders were given to fire at and so on. I don't think that the witness said that they themselves shot. So could Mr. Ierace quote with greater precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I asked that question in leading form because I assumed that it covered territory that was not disputed. Clearly, it is disputed, so I will do it the long way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do it the short long way, please, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to your time in Ozrenska Street, did any member of your platoon take up a position inside the two-storey house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You've told us -- I withdraw that. On the occasions -- on any of the occasions that you observed civilians -- I see that Mr. Piletta-Zanin is on his feet again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please. He is down again, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I venture to stand up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On any of the occasions that you've so far told us about where you observed civilians on the other side of the confrontation line being shot or shot at from individuals on your side of the confrontation line, were any members of your platoon responsible for the shooting?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I do apologise, but I think that Mr. Ierace could tell us what statement by the witness he is referring to exactly. Thank you in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't think he's referring to any statement, but he is putting an initial question. "On any of the occasions that you've so far told us about where you observed civilians," so this is referring to many occasions, and I do remember that on several occasion the witness did. So the objection is denied. Perhaps you would please repeat the question to the witness, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, on any of the occasions that you have so far told us about where you observed civilians on the other side of the confrontation line being shot or shot at from individuals on your side of the confrontation line, were any members of your platoon responsible for the shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: They shot at the two skyscrapers that were underneath us with the weapons that they had, but they were not able to reach the intersections and containers that I mentioned a moment ago. Those were places that were sniped and machine-gunned with the M-84 type of weapon with a larger range.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You've told us that the orders that you and other members of your platoon received were, in effect, to shoot at anything that moved. Did you observe any apparent conflict between those orders and this behaviour by other members of your platoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to the targeting of civilians by members of the sniping unit, you told us that they received their orders at a battalion level. Did you have any reason to doubt that their behaviour in targeting civilians was inconsistent with the orders they had received?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't think I ever noticed that. I wasn't in a position to notice anything of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In responding to questions asked by Mr. President as to why you had not complained of irregularities, you referred to the fruitless outcome of complaints arising from behaviour outside the platoon, if I can put it that way. Did you have any expectation that if you had complained of the targeting of civilians, that such a complaint would be welcomed or properly acted upon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nobody would have done anything at all, taken any positive action. I'm quite certain of that, and that's why I didn't complain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, we are not very flexible today since appointments have been made after 1.00. Would it be possible to finish in one minute or do you think -- otherwise, we would have to recall the witness, and would you please consider whether this is really necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would it be -- Mr. President, I'm also conscious of the fact that we have to formally tender the exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I think -- I would suggest to you that we would do that first thing tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In that case, Mr. President, could you allow me, say, two or three minutes and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have to look at -- because appointments have been outside the courtroom, outside the detention facilities, for the accused. So would you please then really as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were asked questions, sir, about the firing of weaponry from Ozrenska Street. Earlier you gave evidence that there were tanks and an APC at Ozrenska Street. Did you ever see either of that type of weaponry fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were asked about the position of the confrontation lines at Ozrenska Street between June 1992 and May of 1993. Are you aware as to whether there were any offensives along the Ozrenska Street front lines by either side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there any change in the confrontation lines at Ozrenska Street during the period that you were a platoon member, although not necessarily when you were stationed at Ozrenska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were some slight changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And finally, you've said that food was distributed from a house at Ozrenska Street. Do you know where the food was cooked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS D [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was in a barracks in Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I have a very practical solution. We know why we stop at 1.00. Perhaps if this would be possible to continue for three, up to five minutes with all the technicalities and allow the accused to leave the courtroom. If that is okay as far as the Defence is concerned -- yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You know the reasons why, and I'm very concerned that the appointment would -- so --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm touched, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: General Galic, so we'll continue for five minutes with technicalities, and you'll be brought to your appointment, and I hope it will not -- the outcome will not disappoint you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think since there are no further questions for the witness, that the witness may leave the courtroom. I saw that he was raising his hand, so if there's any -- well, your examination has been finished by now, Mr. D. If there is anything you'd like to add, if it does not go to the substance of what has been discussed here, please tell me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should just like to stress once again that during this trial I have spoken the truth --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and in speaking the truth, I -- and in testifying, I did not wish to say anything against people of other ethnic groups to which I do not belong. I just testified on the basis of everything that I have seen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. D, in the absence of the accused, I would not like to touch upon whatever issue which to the substance of the case. I think until now we did not. Of course we do understand that you were strictly observing the solemn declaration you made at the beginning. This is the end of your examination. I'd like to thank you for having come --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'd like to thank you for coming that far away and informing this Chamber about what you know on those subjects you have been examined about. Before leaving the courtroom, I think that we have to -- well, either we wait or we have to do the curtains down. So if you -- I think that -- there is no one on the right-hand side, so -- especially the other side is important, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm afraid we'll have to wait until the curtains are up again. It takes a bit more than five minutes, but ... I think once one curtain is up, it's public again. So I'd like to continue. No, please continue, but there was no reason for me to stop any more. I think that all the exhibits -- all the documents tendered into evidence, if admitted, it will be admitted under seal because the name of the witness is on, I would say, yes, all the documents. So we have P3637, a set of five maps premarked, and the same set of maps, 3637D, with additional markings made during examination-in-chief and cross-examination. No objections, so that's admitted. Then we have P289, military booklet and additional leaflets. In relation to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to that, Mr. President, there is an English translation that is part of the exhibit list, and I think the Trial Chamber would be assisted by that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that would be P289.1. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's admitted as well. Then we have photographs shown to the witness. Although there have been five photographs circulating, only three have been used. That's P3251, P3252, and P3253. That's admitted in evidence as well. Then, finally, we have a manual on weaponry. That's P3638, and that's also admitted into evidence. I just received a copy of a letter concerning Witness L. May I assume that there's no specific reason to -- that it was given to us right now? Does it need any further discussion or --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. That's the letter that was faxed to the Defence late last night from the Prosecution. It informs the Defence of forthcoming exhibits and evidence. The Defence and I have arranged a meeting at 2.00 this afternoon. It is simply a copy for Your Honours. It was handed over at the beginning of the trial this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. So if there's no other issues to be discussed at this moment, we'll adjourn until tomorrow morning at 9.00 in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 23rd day of January, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.10 p.m.,
